correctness.rationale: Invariance of any compactly supported measure with µ(x=0)=0, tested against bounded smooth truncations h_L(log|x|), gives ⟨y⟩=1 even when support accumulates at x=0. Stationary Lie identities for y,z,x²,y²,yz,z² yield ⟨x²⟩=1, ⟨z⟩=⟨yz⟩=0, Var(y)=⟨z²⟩, ⟨x²z⟩=a⟨z²⟩; expanding the square proves Var(x²)-a²Var(y)=⟨(x²-1-a z)²⟩≥0. On equality the analytic observable g=x²-1-a z vanishes along almost every orbit and g′=(2x²-a)(1-y)-a g; the analytic zero product forces either y≡1 or x²≡a/2, each giving only equilibria (±1,1,0). Divergence 1-y-a and (log|x|)′=1-y imply exact Jacobian det=e^-at|x(t)/x0|, hence periodic transverse multiplier product and stationary Lyapunov sum -a (where defined). A=2-ε² Hopf normal form q=log|x| yields cubic solvability A_amplitude²=2 and ω_2=-1/6. Independent symbolic differentiation checks g_{ε²}=cos2θ−sin2θ and its mean square 1, proving squared defect~(2-a)²; leading Var(y)~2-a and Var(x²)~4(2-a). Numerical data are not used as proofs of Hopf existence.
